chunks: A number of our companions informed us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from Abu Jamila, from Sa'd ibn Tarif, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) passed by a man and said: 'What did you do with your wife?' He said: 'I divorced her, O Messenger of God.' He asked: 'Without any wrongdoing (on her part)?' He said: 'Without any wrongdoing.'

Then [the narrator] said: The man got married again. The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) passed by him and said: 'You got married?' He said: 'Yes.' Then he said to him some time after: 'What did you do with your wife?' He said: 'I divorced her.' He asked: 'Without any wrongdoing?' He said: 'Without any wrongdoing.'

Then the man got married again. The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) passed by him and said: 'You got married?' He said: 'Yes.' Then he said to him some time after: 'What did you do with your wife?' He said: 'I divorced her.' He asked: 'Without any wrongdoing?' He said: 'Without any wrongdoing.' So the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Indeed God — Mighty and Majestic — hates, or curses, every taster (dhawwaq) from among the men and every taster (dhawwaqah) from among the women.'

key_terms.ذَوَّاق / ذَوَّاقَة: Taster — one who frequently marries and divorces without cause, treating spouses as objects to be sampled
key_terms.مِنْ غَيْرِ سُوءٍ: Without wrongdoing — divorcing without moral justification or fault on the spouse's part
key_terms.يُبْغِضُ أَوْ يَلْعَنُ: Hates or curses — the narrator's uncertainty (أَوْ) between two words of escalating severity, both indicating divine displeasure

ai.seo_question: What does Islam say about repeatedly marrying and divorcing without cause?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) narrates a hadith from the Prophet (SAWW) in which the Prophet three times encounters the same man who has divorced his wife without cause and remarried. After the third divorce, the Prophet pronounces that God hates — or curses — every dhawwaq (man) and dhawwaqa (woman), meaning those who habitually marry and divorce without moral justification, treating marriage as something to be sampled and discarded. This teaching condemns serial divorce as a grave moral failing, not merely a legal question, framing it as something that incurs divine displeasure. In early Islamic society, where divorce was legally accessible to men, this hadith establishes that legal permissibility does not equal moral approval, and repeatedly dissolving marriages without cause is detestable to God.
word_analysis: taster (one who frequently marries and divorces)
taster (woman who frequently marries and divorces)

en.hubeali: تَمَّ كِتَابُ الْعَقِيقَةِ وَ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ وَ يَلِيهِ كِتَابُ الطَّلَاقِ . (This) completes the Book of al Aqeeqa, and the Praise is for Allahazwj, Lordazwj of the Worlds, and it would be followed by the Book of Divorce. A number of our companions informed us, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Abu Jameela, from Sa’ad Bin Tareyf, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’farasws having said: ‘Rasool-Allahsaww passed by a man, so hesaww said: ‘What did you do (with) your wife?’ He said, ‘I divorced her, O Rasool-Allahsaww!’ Hesaww said: ‘Without any wrongdoing (on her part)?’ He said, ‘Without any wrongdoing’.

Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The man got re-married, so the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> passed by him, so he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘You got married?’ He said, ‘Yes’. Then he<sup>saww</sup> said after that, ‘What did you do (with) your wife?’ He said, ‘I divorced her’. He<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Without any wrongdoing (on her part)?’ He said, ‘Without any wrongdoing’.

Then the man got re-married, so the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> passed by him, so he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘You got married?’ So he said, ‘Yes’. Then he<sup>saww</sup> said to him after that: ‘What did you do (with) your wife?’ He said, ‘I divorced her’. He<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Without any wrongdoing (on her part)?’ He said, ‘Without any wrongdoing’.
So Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Hates, or Curses every taster from the men, and every taster from the women’.
en.sarwar: 1. Narrated to us certain persons of our people from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from abu Jamilah from Sa‘d ibn Tarif who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that once the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, passed by a man and asked, ’How is your wife doing?’ He said, ‘I have divorced her, O Messenger of Allah.’ He (the Messenger of Allah) asked, ‘Did you do it without her misbehaving?’ He replied, ‘Yes, it was without her misbehaving.’

He (the Imam) said that he married and the Holy Prophet, passed by and asked, ‘Have you got married?’ He replied, ‘Yes, I have married.’ He (the Messenger of Allah) afterward asked, ‘How is your wife?’ He replied, ‘I have divorced her.’ He (the Messenger of Allah) asked, ‘Did you divorce her without her misbehaving?’ He replied, ‘Yes, it was without her misbehaving.’

The man then got married and the Holy Prophet, passed by and asked, ‘Have you got married?’ Afterward he (the Messenger of Allah) asked about his wife and he replied, ‘I divorced her.’ He (the Messenger of Allah) asked, ‘Did you do without her misbehaving?’ He replied, ‘Yes, it was without her misbehaving.’

The Messenger of Allah then said, ‘Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, hates or condemns every man who divorces hastily (like an epicure who keeps tasting this and that food) and every woman who is as such.’”
